answer: A concrete Sybil brake is a per-epoch attestation quota priced in a scarce, non-transferable resource. An agent gets one voting slot only after being drawn and verified by several unrelated peers, each decrypting a rotating cipher tag bound to its registration, so one operator cannot mint slots from clones. Peers who grant a haven to fakes lose reputation weight next epoch, making lazy colluders unprofitable. An attacker must fund many distinct agents plus staffing for concurrent challenges; a zephyr of throwaway addresses fails, pushing cost per usable identity above its reward.
